release_lag_limitation.text: Real release lags are UNKNOWN. The model assumes data for month M−2 are available at a decision in month M, which leaves about 45 days (median 44; 31 to 59 across decisions); `outputs/release_lag_check.md` uses the stricter shortest window minus one day (30 days). File update dates give only upper bounds on the release lag (true lag ≤ bound): inflation 1 day; exports 66 days; imports 66 days; corporate lending 24 days; household lending 24 days; consumption 37 days. For exports the update date belongs to the edition ending 2026-07; the later rows up to 2026-08 come from a newer edition whose publication date is UNKNOWN. For imports the update date belongs to the edition ending 2026-07; the later rows up to 2026-08 come from a newer edition whose publication date is UNKNOWN. Look-ahead cannot be excluded for 89 of 89 decisions for exports and imports (and for 15 of 89 decisions for consumption). The nearest existing check is RB07 ("Ordered logit: release lag 3 months", which shifts all factors): benchmark winner Model beats Hold, survives No; a check that shifts only the trade series was not run. Revision status of all series is UNKNOWN.

decision_rule.named_user: a bank treasury analyst who, before an NBK base-rate meeting, needs to know whether the model shows a distinguishable tilt in rate pressure
decision_rule.rule: if the 95% band of the score moves entirely above 0 (or entirely below 0), then flag a hawkish (or dovish) tilt and review rate-sensitive exposures before the next decision, because only then is the sign of the pressure distinguishable from balance, given a band about 0.883 score points wide.
